names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 8 Μαΐου, «Όσιος Αρσένιος ο εν τη Λαύρα του Κιέβου ασκήσας», with the rank word left off. No Slavonic form is recorded: saint.gr prints none.

Read out of the Охридски пролог's heading for 8. мај ст. ст., „Преподобни Арсеније Трудољубиви.“ Преподобни is the `venerable` this folder already carries in `types` and `honorific.js` composes back; **Трудољубиви — the industrious, the lover of labour — is kept**, because it is not a rank word in BRIEF-SERBIAN.md §5's table, `honorific.js` does not compose it, and it is the one thing on the page that tells him from the day's other Arsenius. **Keeping it is what holds this folder out of the fold `arsenius-the-great` and `arsenius-of-corfu` now share**, which was measured and not assumed: the bare «Арсеније» would have made a third. „Монах кијевски“ is the body's second sentence and the lavra is the English name's, so neither is in the form. That is the second time in two days that the Prologue printed two men of one name on one day and gave one of them a by-name.

The heading of the calendar’s name page 268 for 8 мая ст. ст., «Преподобный Арсений Трудолюбивый», with the rank word left off. The day’s own line declines him «Арсения трудолюбивого … Печерских», lower-cased; one of his two life pages titles him more fully, «Преподобный Арсений Печерский, Трудолюбивый».

floruit.note: saint.gr: «Ο Όσιος Αρσένιος, λάτρης της εργασίας, έζησε κατά τον 14ο αιώνα μ.Χ.» The page gives no year of birth and no year of death, only that he fell asleep in peace.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 8 мая ст. ст. — «Прпп. Пимена постника (XII) и Арсения трудолюбивого (XIV), Печерских.»

attestations.note: The line names two men of the Caves and the corpus keeps both; the other, `pimen-the-faster-of-the-caves`, already carries a venerated russian row on 27 августа ст. ст., so BRIEF-RUSSIAN §4 forbids touching it and this upgrade is for one of the two only. Both of his life pages head him «Дни памяти: 8 мая, 28 августа (Печер.(Д))», the second being the synaxis of the fathers of the Farther Caves; that is a day the day page does not repeat, so it is a note here and nothing was moved for it. `dates` is unchanged: both lives say only «жил в XIV веке», the fourteenth century the folder already holds, and neither gives a year. The day page prints two hymns under his name; the troparion of глас 8 is the common of a venerable, printed word for word under `arsenius-the-great` on the same day, and the hymn’s source line says so. azbyka.ru was not read. Read 8 October 2026.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (30 September 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 8ης Μαΐου — «Όσιος Αρσένιος ο εν τη Λαύρα του Κιέβου ασκήσας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 8 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. **Three Arsenii and a Cassian stand on this one day** and they are distinguished by the page's own epithets, not by any reading of mine: the Great at Canopus in 445, the Varnakovite in Phokis in 1111, the fool-for-Christ of Novgorod in 1570, and this one in the Caves of Kyiv in the fourteenth century. **None of the corpus's nine Kyiv-Caves folders is an Arsenius.** `wonderworker` is the page's own: «ο Χριστός του έδωσε το χάρισμα να επιτελεί θαύματα». No relics, no hymn, no place of burial.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 21.05.2026 (8. мај ст. ст.) — „Преподобни Арсеније Трудољубиви.“

attestations.note: **The day is Julian 8 May, the same menologion day the Greek keeps him on, and this is the second account of him this corpus has read.** No row was moved; the Romanian calendar has never held him. **The identification is the by-name, the city and the century together**: „Преподобни Арсеније Трудољубиви. Монах кијевски.“ against saint.gr's «Όσιος Αρσένιος ο εν τη Λαύρα του Κιέβου ασκήσας», whose life reads «Ο Όσιος Αρσένιος, λάτρης της εργασίας, έζησε κατά τον 14ο αιώνα μ.Χ.» — a lover of work, which is what Трудољубиви says, a monk of Kyiv, and the fourteenth century in both books. **He is not the day's other Arsenius**: the Prologue prints both on this one day, „Преподобни Арсеније Велики.“ and this one, which is two commemorations on one calendar on one day and so two men by this corpus's settled rule — and it is also how each was identified. **NO DATE WAS TOUCHED**: „Подвизавао се и упокојио у XIV веку“ gives the same fourteenth century the folder's `floruit` already holds from saint.gr, so there was nothing to add and nothing to narrow. New to the corpus from this page, and it is all of it new: that he **never gave himself any rest but laboured without ceasing**, and that he **took food only once a day, after sunset**. **This folder had no Slavonic form at all** — its own name note says saint.gr prints none — and now has a Serbian one. `types` was not touched: Преподобни is the `venerable` it already holds, and Трудољубиви is a by-name, not a rank. **No `locations`**: Kyiv is in the body as the city he was a monk of, and the folder's English name already carries the lavra. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Слез твоих теченьми пустыни безплодное возделал еси,/ и иже из глубины воздыханьми во сто трудов уплодоносил еси,/ и был еси светильник вселенней, сияя чудесы, Арсение отче наш,/ моли Христа Бога спастися душам нашим.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 8 мая ст. ст., «Тропарь преподобного Арсения трудолюбивого», глас 8 — the common of a venerable with his name set into it, printed word for word under the other Arsenius of the same day, «Тропарь преподобного Арсения», with one line break more

english.text: By the streams of thy tears thou didst make the barren wilderness fruitful, and by thy sighs out of the deep thou didst bring forth a hundredfold in labours, and thou becamest a lamp to the whole world, shining with wonders, O Arsenius our father. Pray to Christ God that our souls may be saved.

hymns.text: Яже на земли оставль, Христовым стопам последовал еси тепле/ и, Того, славне, на рамо взем честный крест,/ умертвил еси труды постническими телесныя желания, треблаженне./ Темже зовем ти: радуйся, отче Арсение.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 8 мая ст. ст., «Кондак преподобного Арсения трудолюбивого», глас 8 — the hymn that tells the two Arseniuses of the day apart: it sings the labours of fasting and names no city

english.text: Leaving behind the things of earth, thou didst follow fervently in the footsteps of Christ; and taking up his honoured cross upon thy shoulder, O glorious one, thou didst put to death the desires of the body by the labours of fasting, O thrice-blessed. Therefore do we cry to thee: rejoice, O father Arsenius.
